chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from his father, from Sulayman al-Ja'fari, who raised it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
There is no household to whom thirty sheep return [in the evening] except that the angels do not cease to guard them until the morning.

key_terms.الْمَلَائِكَةُ: The angels — divine beings assigned as guardians
key_terms.تَحْرُسُهُمْ: Guard/protect them — continuous overnight angelic protection
key_terms.تَرُوحُ: Return/come in the evening — refers to the evening return of livestock to the household
key_terms.ثَلَاثُونَ شَاةً: Thirty sheep — the threshold number stipulated for the blessing
key_terms.رَفَعَهُ: Raised/elevated it — hadith transmission term indicating a gap in the chain

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the blessing of keeping thirty sheep?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) describes a divine blessing: any household that keeps thirty sheep will have angels standing guard over them throughout the night. This hadith is found in the chapter on sheep (al-ghanam) in al-Kafi and reflects the Islamic tradition of linking animal husbandry — particularly the keeping of small livestock — to divine protection and blessing. The early Muslim community understood the keeping of sheep as a virtuous livelihood connecting them to prophetic practice, and this narration assures such households of angelic protection each night.
